title: The smell, taste, sight, or thought of food can start stomach juice
summary: OpenStax describes a cephalic phase in which wanting a food triggers gastric juice before the food arrives.
body: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology says secretion of gastric juice is controlled by nerves and hormones, in three phases. The cephalic, or reflex, phase is brief and happens before food enters the stomach. The smell, taste, sight, or thought of food can trigger it. Signals from the nose or the taste buds go to the brain, which sends signals back that increase gastric secretion so the stomach is ready. The textbook says this extra secretion is a conditioned reflex that occurs when a person likes or wants that particular food, and that depression and loss of appetite can suppress it. Paraphrased from the 25 April 2013 text.
